asof: Settles Tue 10 Nov 2026 · written Wed 11 Nov
headline: Hot core CPI and Waller's 50bp talk lift the reds 22–23.5bp; the U7 peak at 4.66% now prices three hikes.
summary: The strip sold off hard on Tuesday, led by the reds: M7 rose 23.5bp to 4.645%, U7 22.5bp to 4.66%, H7 22bp to 4.535% and Z7 20bp, while Z6 rose 12bp to 4.285%, U6 just 0.5bp to 3.925% and the 2029 contracts 11–12.5bp to 4.435–4.465%. That more than reverses last Thursday's rally: from the 30 October settle Z6 is now 14bp higher, H7 18bp, M7 16.5bp and U7 14bp, against only 4–6.5bp in Z8–Z9. The peak stays in SR3U7 at 4.66%, 78bp over the 3.88% SOFR fixing, with 22.5bp of easing priced from there to Z9. Roughly three hikes is more than the consensus of a December move plus one more in early 2027.
drivers: Core CPI tops forecasts for a third month

October CPI rose 0.4% against 0.3% expected and core 0.3% against 0.2%, with shelter accounting for over 30% of the gain; no annual rate was published because of last year's shutdown. The 2-year yield jumped 17–19bp to about 4.73%, its biggest rise since April 2025, and in SR3 H7–U7 rose 22–23.5bp in rate.
Waller and Logan put 50bp on the table

Before the data Waller said a core print of 0.3% or more would make him consider a half-point December hike, and Logan said the Fed needs at least another 50bp before pausing. FedWatch moved to about a 99% chance of a December hike with roughly 11% odds of 50bp, up from zero; Z6 rose 12bp and U6/Z6 widened 11.5bp to +36bp.

The $42bn 10-year stopped at 5.020%, tailing the 5.010% when-issued by 1bp, with bid-to-cover down to 2.46 from 2.77 and indirects at 61.2% against 80.3% last time. The 10-year yield rose about 14bp to 5.00%, but the curve still flattened: Z8 rose 13.5bp and Z9 11bp, well under the reds.
Cheaper oil keeps the greens behind

Brent fell another $1.08 to settle at $91.49, its lowest since 31 August, after US officials played down further strikes on Iran. Lower energy keeps the market pricing cuts after the peak: easing from U7 to Z9 doubled to 22.5bp from 11bp on Monday, and Z7/Z8 fell 6.5bp to −13bp.
spreads: The front and reds steepened sharply. U6/Z6 widened 11.5bp to +36bp and Z6/H7 10bp to +25bp (+4bp on the month), while H7/M7 rose 1.5bp to +11bp (−1.5bp month-to-date) and M7/U7 slipped 1bp to +1.5bp (−2.5bp); U7/Z7 fell 2.5bp to −4.5bp, so U7 is now the peak by 1.5bp over M7 and 4.5bp over Z7. Z6/Z7 widened 8bp to +33bp (−2bp on the month) and Z6/M7 11.5bp to +36bp (+2.5bp). Past the peak the inversion deepened: Z7/H8 and H8/M8 fell to −4bp each, Z7/Z8 6.5bp to −13bp and U7/Z8 9bp to −17.5bp (−5.5bp and −7.5bp on the month), with Z8/Z9 at −5bp (−2.5bp) and the late-2028 and 2029 consecutive spreads between −2.5bp and −0.5bp. The H7/M7/U7 fly rose 2.5bp to +9.5bp and M7/U7/Z7 1.5bp to +6bp (+1bp and −0.5bp on the month). Week-to-date, measured from Friday's settle, H7/M7 is +1.5bp, Z7/Z8 −9.5bp and U7/Z8 −13bp.
fed: The latest weekday fed funds futures snapshot is Monday's, before CPI: 20.4bp for the 9 December meeting (an 82% chance of a hike), 27bp by January, 38.1bp by March, 49.6bp by June and a 51bp peak by September 2027 (implied EFFR 4.39%). That is up from 19bp, 24bp, 34bp, 43.9bp and 47bp on Friday, and against 2 November (18.3bp, 25.5bp, 38.8bp, 53.4bp, 57bp peak) and the 30 October month-end (17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp, 57bp) December and January are higher but the mid-2027 path had still been lower. Tuesday's SR3 settles leave that snapshot behind: with SOFR and EFFR both fixing at 3.88%, U7 at 4.66% sits 27bp over the 4.39% ZQ peak, and Z6 at 4.285% is 13.5bp over Monday's January ZQ rate, consistent with the roughly 99% December odds and the small chance of 50bp that FedWatch showed after the data. Most bank economists and GSAM call December a firm hike and September's projections show one more move this year, while Logan wants at least 50bp more; three hikes to the U7 peak is at the hawkish end of that range, and the next ZQ snapshot should confirm how much of the move holds.

ideas.title: Stay short the H7/M7 calendar spread (fade a longer hiking run)
ideas.why: Open at +11bp, 2bp against entry: H7 rose 22bp and M7 23.5bp in rate, so the CPI selloff added a little to hikes after March as well as before it. Waller's and Logan's push for faster moves argues for front-loading rather than a longer cycle, which should narrow the March–June gap; we keep the stop at +13bp, giving 8bp to target against 2bp of risk.
ideas.risk: A firm PPI on Friday or hot retail sales could extend pricing of hikes past April and push the spread through +13bp.

ideas.title: Z7/Z8 target hit; roll the hedge to U7/Z8
ideas.why: Z7/Z8 fell 6.5bp to −13bp on Tuesday, hitting its −13bp target for a 5bp gain from −8bp entry, so we take profit. The same exposure now sits best at the peak: U7 rose 22.5bp against 13.5bp in Z8, taking U7/Z8 to −17.5bp, and it protects the core if hawkish data keeps lifting the 2027 path while cheaper oil anchors 2028. 5.5bp to target against 3.5bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: A sharp fall in stocks or a soft PPI that revives the haven bid in the reds would lift the spread back above −14bp.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through refunding settlement

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 rose only 0.5bp to 3.925% on a day the reds moved 22–23.5bp, against the 3.88% SOFR fixing for 9 November, 2bp under the 3.90% interest on reserves and level with EFFR. Only its last week sees the 9 December decision, so even a 50bp hike is worth under 2bp on the contract, while refunding notes settle on 16 November.
ideas.risk: If refunding settlement tightens funding, SOFR could print back near 3.95% and cost a couple of bp.

watch: Cash bond market closed and no SOFR fixing; SR3 liquidity thin after Tuesday's 22–23.5bp move in the reds.
